run.runNote: Phase 1 Step 1-2 for the transformers target. The task brief described a phone/desktop connectivity project (socket protocol, plugins, predefined commands); that description does not match this source tree. The tree at transformers_vuln (commit 87a6cf4, the CodeQL database creation sha) is the HuggingFace transformers machine-learning library. All exploration, evidence, and query generation below are derived from the actual source code, not from the brief's description. Per experiment constraints, the PyVul ground-truth files present in the tree (confirmed_vulns.json, CVE application report, cmd_sinks.csv, cmd_safe_sinks.csv) were NOT read; no vulnerability locations, CVE diffs, or descriptions were consulted, and no rules target known locations.

target.projectDescription: State-of-the-art machine-learning library for PyTorch/TensorFlow/JAX: model implementations, tokenizers/processors, training (Trainer), inference pipelines (text/audio/vision), and a setuptools argparse-based CLI (transformers-cli, transformers.onnx) that shells out to git, git-lfs, ffmpeg and optimum.exporters.onnx.

evidence: 2781 .py files in the source tree; src/transformers/ package (1516 files in the DB source archive) plus setup.py, hubconf.py, conftest.py

database.coverageNote: The database covers the WHOLE repository, not just the library: the DB source archive contains 1516 files under src/transformers/ and 903 files under tests/, plus examples/, utils/ (CI scripts) and docs. Both extraction queries therefore apply a path filter restricting candidate rows to src/transformers/ (see extraction.exclusions).

framework.notes: No web framework detected; all framework scores are below the 0.50 threshold, so no framework reference is loaded. The externally reachable surfaces relevant to CWE-78 are (1) the transformers-cli / transformers.onnx argparse command layer and (2) the git-lfs custom transfer agent that receives line-delimited JSON on stdin. inputBoundaryInventory.summary: This is a library, not a network service: there are no listening sockets in src/transformers. Attacker-influenced data for CWE-78 enters through (1) CLI arguments of transformers-cli / transformers.onnx / Trainer scripts (argparse, HfArgParser, sys.argv), (2) line-delimited JSON that git-lfs writes to the stdin of the lfs-multipart-upload transfer agent (oid, path, action.href, action.header fields), (3) environment variables (WANDB_*, COMET_*, MLFLOW_*, TRANSFORMERS_*, XLA_*), (4) JSON decoded from hub-downloaded config/preprocessor files, and (5) values returned by network fetches (requests, huggingface_hub). Command-execution sinks concentrate in the CLI/lfs layer (subprocess with an f-string command in lfs, a shell=True ' '.join(cmd_line) in the ONNX exporter, fixed argv lists for git/git-lfs/ninja version probes) and in the audio pipelines that spawn ffmpeg. In this snapshot none of the exec sites shell-quotes its interpolated values (no shlex.quote anywhere; the only shlex use is testing_utils.py:1596 shlex.split on a generated string).

sanitizerObservations: No shlex.quote / pipes.quote / shell-escaping wrapper exists at any exec site in this snapshot; the only shlex usage is testing_utils.py:1596 shlex.split (tokenization of a generated command, not escaping of interpolated values).

Most exec sites use fixed list argv without shell (user.py git/git-lfs probes, import_utils.py ninja probe, audio ffmpeg_command lists) - argument-list invocation, a structural (not proof-level) mitigating shape for labeling.

lfs.py exec commands interpolate only in-repo constants and the module-level LFS_MULTIPART_UPLOAD_COMMAND; the externally controlled value at that site is local_path, passed as cwd=, not as part of the command string.
onnx/__main__.py:59 joins CLI-derived values into a shell=True command with no quoting - recorded as candidate only; final vulnerability judgment is deferred to taint analysis and labeling.
inputBoundaryInventory.nonVulnerabilityNote: The predefined CLI functionality (transformers-cli commands, ffmpeg pipeline helpers, version probes, test helpers) is normal intended functionality and is NOT automatically treated as a vulnerability; these are recorded only as candidate boundaries for labeling.

extraction.executionPlan: codeql query run (sequential, one at a time) followed by codeql bqrs decode --format=csv; NOT database analyze / SARIF
extraction.metadataForm: plain multi-column select queries carrying @name/@description/@id/@tags only; intentionally no @kind problem (wrong shape for multi-column candidate tables) and no @kind table (not assumed to exist). Raw BQRS output is decoded directly to CSV.
columnContract: node (location-backed AST node; decodes as file:line:col)
arg_index (0-based positional argument index, -1 when not applicable)
match_kind ('api' = resolved real API call via API graphs, 'ast' = syntax-level match)

matchKindSemantics.api: call resolved through semmle.python.ApiGraphs (API::moduleImport(...).getMember(...).getACall()); alias-aware, only genuine resolved calls into external modules
matchKindSemantics.ast: pure AST shape match (attribute/name text, syntactic module prefix, receiver name); catches dynamic or unresolved shapes that API graphs miss and is subject to name-collision noise

extraction.pathFilter: both queries restrict rows to files under src/transformers/ via a case-insensitive path regexp on the node's absolute file path (the DB covers the whole repo including tests/examples/utils)
exclusions: tests/ (903 files in the DB) and the repo-root examples/, utils/, docs/, .circleci/ trees are excluded by the src/transformers/ path filter (test fixtures, CI scripts and generated code per WORKFLOW noise rules)

generic *.from_pretrained(...) call sites (2112 in src/transformers) are NOT extracted as source rows: they are the model-loading boundary but would dominate the candidate table with a single repeated signature; they are recorded here and can be modeled as a MySummaries taint step in Phase 2 if labeling needs them
logging-only helpers (logger.* / logging.*) are not extracted as candidates
docstring/doctest code (requests.get examples in modeling docstrings) is not real AST and is not matched

uncoveredCases: transformers_cli.py:54 'args.func(args)' - the command factory is attached dynamically via parser.set_defaults(func=lambda args: XCommand(args)); the lambda body target is not resolvable at extraction time. Mitigated by emitting the args.func(args) call as an internal_transfer row plus run()/__init__ handler-param rows for *Command classes.

*.from_pretrained(...) (2112 sites) - the dominant external-data boundary (model id -> hub download -> config.json -> PretrainedConfig kwargs). Excluded from row extraction for volume; a Phase 2 MySummaries step (parameter 0 taint into the loaded config/objects) is the right modeling point.

huggingface_hub and requests library internals are not part of the database; only import-side API-graph resolution is used, so 'return' rows for requests/hf_hub_download mark the boundary, and flow through library internals relies on the later taint configuration.
os.environ.get(...) / os.environ[...] reads are captured at the os.environ attribute node; bound-method (map(os.environ.get, ...)) shapes and os.environb are not modeled.

Bare-name (from-import) execution APIs are only matched for distinctive names (system, popen, getoutput, getstatusoutput); bare call/run/check_call are too collision-prone. In this snapshot every exec site is attribute-qualified (subprocess.*, asyncio.*), so the gap is not exercised.
f-strings (Fstring AST nodes) are only extracted inside functions that directly execute OS commands; f-string usage elsewhere is not a candidate.
Dynamic dispatch via importlib/importlib.importlib, __import__ and getattr(...) is not extracted.
eval/exec dynamic code execution is out of scope for pass 2 (covered by pass 4).

constraintsHonored.notes: No PyVul vulnerability ground truth (confirmed_vulns.json, cmd_sinks.csv, cmd_safe_sinks.csv, CVE application report), CVE fix diffs, or vulnerability descriptions were consulted; candidate families are derived from repository evidence and the loaded language/pattern references only. No rules were added that target known vulnerability locations. Project source, the CodeQL database, and the Augur installation were not modified. Only iris/exploration/detection.json, iris/extraction/sources.ql and iris/extraction/sinks.ql were written; CodeQL execution and LLM labeling are deferred to later steps.
